clue.text: Strikers threaten one dropping out? They can be dismissed on appeal

definitions.text: They can be dismissed on appeal

parts.note: bats are what strike the ball

indicators.note: something dropping out leaves the word it belonged to, so a piece of the threat word is removed

parts.note: to menace is to threaten
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Strikers threatening to walk out, with a wink at those who appeal against dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: MENACE loses ACE. 'Strikers' sounds industrial, but the scene is cricket: batsmen are given out when the umpire upholds a fielder's appeal of 'Howzat?'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter is dismissed when the umpire upholds the fielding side's appeal, so this cryptically describes batsmen.

clue.text: Knocks from Bravo in short made it with Stokes

parts.note: Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is a short form of in
ff stands for fecerunt, Latin for they made it
S is a short form of stokes, a unit of viscosity

explanation.surface: England cricketer Ben Stokes making hits as Bravo looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: Every piece is an abbreviation; Stokes looks like the cricketer but is the unit of viscosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A biff is a blow or punch, so biffs are knocks.

clue.text: Academician's ridiculous to hold up article concerning ink

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for Academician, as in ARA

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: art. is the abbreviation for article
mental is slang for crazy or ridiculous

explanation.surface: A scholar is being absurd in delaying an article about ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like the grammar word A or THE, but here it is the abbreviation art., as in a numbered clause of a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: Atramental is a rare adjective from Latin atramentum, ink, meaning inky or black as ink.

clue.text: Italian cop succeeded getting little resistance in pen

parts.note: S is short for succeeded

indicators.note: in places the resistance letter inside the pen

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, little meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: An Italian policeman found he met little resistance when locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sbirro is Italian for a police officer, used in English for an Italian cop.

clue.text: Issuing ecstasy, smuggler caught leading to fine

indicators.note: issuing means sending out, so the drug's letter leaves the word

parts.note: a mule smuggles drugs across borders
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
CT as an abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A drug mule is caught and fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective or a verb but is a noun, a penalty; 'issuing' means letting the drug's letter go.
explanation.definitionFit: A mulct is a fine or monetary penalty; the word is also a verb meaning to fine.

clue.text: Laments idea oddly to cut European members

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: to cut into is to go inside, so these letters sit within another piece

parts.note: legs are limbs, members of the body

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions

parts.note: first and third letters of idea

explanation.surface: Mourning songs strike an odd idea for slashing European arms and legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegies are mournful poems or songs, laments for the dead.

clue.text: Picture of the Month challenge discontinued

parts.note: mo is a short form of month
vie was once a noun meaning a challenge or bid, a sense now obsolete

explanation.surface: A magazine's 'Picture of the Month' contest has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontinued' marks an obsolete sense, not a deletion: as a noun, vie meant a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is an everyday name for a film, as in going to the pictures.

clue.text: Old lady nursing sick daughter shows restraint across the pond

indicators.note: nursing means cradling, so the old lady holds the other pieces

parts.note: mam is an informal word for mother
ill means sick
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother caring for her ill daughter shows restraint in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' usually means in America; here it is literal, a barrier over a mill pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A milldam is a dam built across a stream to form a millpond, so it restrains the water.

clue.text: Man in house with line disconnected

indicators.note: disconnected means cut off, so the line letter is removed

parts.note: house, or housey-housey, is the game also called lotto or bingo
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A man at home cut off from his phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: House is an old British name for bingo, a game also called lotto.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's first name, so a man in crossword terms.

clue.text: Energy seen around mount in the country

indicators.note: seen around means placed so as to surround, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: vim means energy
Etna is a volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Energy spent climbing a mountain in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Replays concerning Hearts, it's said

indicators.note: it's said points to the way the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: on means concerning, and cores are hearts

explanation.surface: Football replays involving Hearts, the Edinburgh club, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts looks like the Scottish football team, but it means the cores of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Encores are repeated performances given at the audience's demand, so replays.

clue.text: Agitation in Unite upset with Old Bill

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: The trade union Unite is in uproar about the police, the Old Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police, but here Old and Bill are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullition is boiling up, and figuratively a sudden outburst of feeling, so agitation is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Weaker official about to admit abuse

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is placed inside the other
about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the official's short title faces the other way

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
to rail is to rant abusively

explanation.surface: A feeble referee is ready to let abuse go unpunished.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailer is the comparative of frail, meaning less strong, which is what weaker means.

clue.text: Casement's embellishment a spymaster in Special Branch linked with case of eventual uprising

indicators.note: in places the article and spymaster inside the reworked word
special branch here is read as the word branch made special, that is arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: in a down entry something rising reads from bottom to top
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of eventual

explanation.surface: Roger Casement, a spymaster and Special Branch all tangled in a case about an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Special Branch is the British police intelligence unit; Roger Casement was hanged after the 1916 Easter Rising, but casement here is a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A chambranle is the ornamental frame or border around a door, window or fireplace.

clue.text: Free from rain, pretty good bazaar for charity

definitions.meaning: third meaning: a sale or fete held to raise money

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word, not the usual two.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers dry weather, a moderately good standard, and a charity sale or fete.

clue.text: Fate of Charlie on hold

parts.note: a charlie and a clot are both British words for a fool
ho! is an old call meaning stop or hold

explanation.surface: Charlie's destiny is in the balance, put on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fate' looks like a common noun but is one of the three Fates of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho was one of the three Fates of Greek mythology, the one who spun the thread of life.

clue.text: Clever person coloured confectionery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a smart alec, a know-all
second meaning: one of a brand of sugar-coated chocolate sweets

explanation.walkthrough: Smarties are British sugar-shelled chocolate buttons in many colours, a little like M&Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartie is a would-be clever person, and also one sweet from the coloured Smarties brand.

clue.text: Guard in Arab stores ready for Jordan

indicators.note: the words before it are said to store or hold the answer within their run of letters

parts.note: spanning the end of guard, the word in, and the start of Arab

explanation.surface: A sentry inside an Arab warehouse is prepared for Jordan.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is slang for cash, so 'ready for Jordan' means Jordan's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency of Jordan, and ready is slang for cash money.

clue.text: President to prohibit one form of art from Japan

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower
to ban is to prohibit
a means one

explanation.surface: A president moves to ban one kind of Japanese art.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging.

clue.text: Type of dog leads with special attachments getting interest as before

indicators.note: leads are the front parts, so the first letters are taken

parts.note: first letters of special and attachments
usage is an obsolete word for interest on a loan, usury

explanation.surface: Dog leads with special clips now attract interest, as they did before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' suggests dog leads, but it picks first letters. 'As before' marks a sense that is now obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage dog is the informal name for a dachshund, so sausage names a type of dog.

clue.text: Sister in reverse outside wing halves

indicators.note: outside places that piece around the wing word
in reverse means going backwards, so the sibling word is read from its end

parts.note: sib is short for sibling
a wing of a party or church can be a sect, a faction

explanation.surface: A nun backs out of a wing of the convent, halving it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, so bisects is a verb meaning halves.

clue.text: Cheese on grilled meat cut is a Japanese dish

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

indicators.note: grilling cooks and changes food, so the word beside it is rearranged
cut means shortened, so the meat word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheese melted over a cut of grilled meat makes a Japanese dish.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAT cut to MEA and then shuffled gives AME.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young soya beans boiled in the pod, a standard Japanese appetiser.

clue.text: Had snack prepared omitting cold dish

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up afresh, so the letters are rearranged
omitting means leaving out, so the cold letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone had a snack made, without anything cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhansak is a Parsi dish of meat or vegetables cooked with lentils, popular in Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Dishonest Khan unexpectedly retaining power

indicators.note: retaining means keeping inside, so one piece holds the other
something happening unexpectedly is out of its usual order, so the name's letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
vis is Latin for force or power

explanation.surface: A dishonest Khan surprisingly clings to power.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a rogue, so knavish behaviour is roguish and dishonest.

clue.text: Slimmer in supermarket ends with veggie burger

parts.note: Spar is a chain of convenience stores and supermarkets

indicators.note: ends are last letters, so each word gives its final letter

parts.note: last letters of veggie and burger

explanation.surface: A dieter in a supermarket ends up with a veggie burger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slimmer' looks like a noun, a dieter, but it is the adjective: thinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can mean lean or thin, so sparer means thinner, slimmer.

clue.text: Heads to roll in favoured gatherings producing cases

indicators.note: when heads roll people lose their heads, so each word loses its first letter

parts.note: pet as an adjective means favourite
a hui is a Maori gathering or meeting

explanation.surface: Heads will roll at favoured meetings, leading to court cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' tempts the solver towards lawsuits, but the cases are small containers.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or other small articles.

clue.text: Rough breathing in grammar school? It's the fags!

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, here the breathing inside the school

parts.note: GS is an abbreviation for grammar school
asper is the Greek rough breathing mark

explanation.surface: Wheezing at school? Blame the cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag is British slang for a cigarette; a gasper is a cheap one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasper is old British slang for a cigarette, so gaspers are fags.

clue.text: Boat mostly around source of African river such as this one

definitions.text: Boat mostly around source of African river such as this one

indicators.note: around puts the shortened boat outside the other pieces
mostly means not all of it, so the boat word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ship is a large boat

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of African
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boat almost reaches the source of an African river.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIP minus P wraps A and R. The whole clue also describes the answer: the Shari, or Chari, is an African river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shari, also spelt Chari, flows through Central Africa into Lake Chad, so it is an African river.

clue.text: Term for brass handle?

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so the last letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: last letter of brass
a haft is the handle of a knife or tool

explanation.surface: Asking for the name of a brass handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a request for a word, and also gives the word: a shaft is a handle, here perhaps of a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is the long handle of a tool or weapon, so a fair name for a handle.

clue.text: British actress Jane seen in straw hat

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
Jane Asher is an English actress

explanation.surface: A British actress photographed wearing a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A basher is a dialect name for a straw hat, a boater.

clue.text: Ditch husband with expression of pleasure

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
aha is an exclamation of satisfaction

explanation.surface: Dump the husband and enjoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning dump, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall, used as an invisible boundary in landscaped parks.

clue.text: Maid, one indeed for a Sloane

parts.note: a means one
yah is the posh drawled yes of a Sloane Ranger

explanation.surface: A maid agrees, as one would in posh Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a stereotypical upper-class young Londoner from around Sloane Square, whose 'yes' comes out as 'yah'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayah is a nursemaid or lady's maid in India and other former British colonies.

clue.text: Ruler's traditional dress in Thailand not available

indicators.note: in puts the dress inside the country's code letter

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
the sari is the traditional dress of Indian women
NA is the abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A ruler's national costume cannot be bought in Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was a Russian empress, the female equivalent of a tsar, so a ruler.

clue.text: Experiences of migrants beginning with hope and ending with rescue at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word migrants taken as written; of only links

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of hope

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of rescue

explanation.surface: Migrants set off full of hope and end up being rescued at sea, a grim experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightmares are terrifying ordeals, a fair description of perilous sea crossings.

clue.text: Parts of ground in sporting venues not given a name?

indicators.note: with no name, the abbreviation for name has to be dropped from the word

parts.note: arenas are sporting venues

explanation.surface: Sections of a stadium in anonymous sports venues.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name; ARENAS loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Areas are regions or sections of land, so parts of ground.

clue.text: Avoid confronting stores about water parsnip

indicators.note: to store something is to hold it within

parts.note: to skirt an issue is to avoid confronting it
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone shirking a confrontation hoards things about a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirret is a perennial plant of the carrot family grown for its edible roots, also called water parsnip.
